official_sources.title: GDAL raster band value semantics
official_sources.finding: A raster band may carry a data type, NoData value, validity mask, unit type and scale/offset metadata; meaningful values such as heights can require applying scale and offset.
official_sources.limitation: Metadata presence does not prove that it is correct; the selected band, scale, offset, unit and mask must be recorded and checked against the official product.

official_sources.title: GDAL unscale operation and output type requirement
official_sources.finding: GDAL defines unscaled_value = scaled_raw_value * scale + offset and notes that the output data type often must be reset when applying unscale.
official_sources.limitation: Assigning scale or offset metadata alone does not modify pixel values; integer output types can truncate or overflow decoded elevations.

official_sources.title: GDAL exact versus approximate raster statistics
official_sources.finding: gdalinfo exposes separate exact statistics and approximate-statistics modes, along with minimum/maximum, histogram and checksum options.
official_sources.limitation: Approximate statistics can use overviews or subsets and are unsuitable as authoritative parcel minima or maxima.

official_sources.title: GDAL band validity masks
official_sources.finding: GDAL provides a per-band mask interface to distinguish valid and invalid pixels independently of the sample value.
official_sources.limitation: Ignoring internal, external or alpha-derived masks can admit invalid samples even when their numeric values appear plausible.

official_sources.title: GDAL raw NoData and integer precision caveat
official_sources.finding: GDAL states that a band NoData value is returned in raw, unscaled form and that Int64 or UInt64 NoData can be lossy when read through a double-valued API.
official_sources.limitation: NoData comparison must occur in the correct raw domain and with the correct typed API before applying scale and offset.

official_sources.title: GDAL VRT scaling and mask propagation
official_sources.finding: VRT sources may apply scaling, masks, NoData substitution and data-type conversion; source minima and maxima can also trigger whole-dataset analysis for nonlinear scaling.
official_sources.limitation: A VRT can alter values without changing the underlying source file, so the complete VRT graph and selected source band must be included in provenance.

official_sources.title: OGC GeoTIFF vertical CRS and unit requirements
official_sources.finding: For elevation models GeoTIFF supports a horizontal CRS plus VerticalGeoKey; user-defined vertical CRS records require citation, vertical unit and vertical datum metadata.
official_sources.limitation: A horizontal CRS alone is insufficient to establish the elevation reference; missing vertical keys require an official external product specification or fail-closed handling.

official_sources.title: OGC WKT2 vertical CRS axis and length unit
official_sources.finding: WKT2 represents static vertical CRSs with a vertical reference frame, an up-oriented axis and an explicit length unit such as metre.
official_sources.limitation: Unit and axis direction do not by themselves identify the geoid or datum realization; the full CRS identifier and provenance must be retained.
